sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The second parable is of a small infant with whom the father wants to play face-to-face, requiring the father to lower his hands to lift the child, which is an external preparation for the subsequent inner closeness.

translations.translation: And the second parable is of a suckling infant and small child, whose father wants to delight with him face-to-face, and the child is small,
the father must lower his hands etc. to lift his small son, so that he can delight with him in close proximity face-to-face.
For the lifting of the child is only an external matter,
and it is only a preparation for the inner closeness that follows afterward
(the delights etc.).
And behold, the source of this parable is in Ohr HaTorah of the Mitteler Rebbe,
and there an addition is found
(which was not copied in the maamar),
that the small child "delights in his beard"
(of the father).
And it can be said that in this is hinted,
that the drawing down of the encompassing light
(which precedes the inner influence)
is above the chain of descent,
for "beard" refers to the thirteen tikkunei dikna,
the thirteen attributes of mercy that are above the chain of descent.
Nevertheless, they have some connection to the chain of descent,
as it is written,
"Remember Your mercies... for they are from of old"
[therefore they are called "measures," from the term "measurement"].
Also, it is known regarding hairs that they are merely an illumination.
However, through the inner influence that follows afterward
(even though it is lower than the level of the encompassing light)
the Essence that is above the encompassing light is drawn down
(in the manner explained above in section 1 regarding the superiority of the union of Zeir Anpin and Nukvah
(which is an inner union)
over the union of Abba and Imma, as explained by the Tzemach Tzedek in many places
regarding this).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: In divine service, the initial work each day is prayer, which is a general connection followed by an inner connection that draws Divinity into all physical matters, as explained through the Baal Shem Tov's teaching on not greeting before prayer.

translations.translation: And likewise it is in divine service
(as explained in the maamar),
that the beginning of a person's service each day is the work of prayer,
as it is written,
"Cease from man, whose soul is in his nostrils, for of what account is he?"
Do not read "bamah" (of what account) but "bamah" (a high place/altar),
and according to the Alter Rebbe and the Rebbe Maharash,
before prayer a person is considered like a "bamah" (an altar for idolatry).
And "prayer" is a term meaning connection,
that through prayer a person connects to Divinity.
And the order of prayer is,
that first there must be a general closeness
(an external drawing down)
[as its matter is explained in the maamar],
and afterward an inner closeness is made,
where the person connects to Divinity in such a way that he draws Divinity into all his physical matters.
And this will be understood
[that through prayer at the beginning of the day he is able to connect all physical matters and make them vessels for Divinity]
based on what the Baal Shem Tov explained
regarding the prohibition of greeting before prayer,
which is like what is stated in the writings of the Arizal
regarding honoring the older brother,
that it is because "a spirit is left within him,"
that in the first son there is more of the father's spirit than in the other sons,
and all the other sons receive from the father's spirit through the first son.
And because of the father's spirit in the older brother, they are obligated to honor him just as they are obligated in honoring the father
[therefore this law is derived
from the verse,
"Honor your father" specifically,
for honoring the older brother is included in honoring the father].
And likewise it is regarding a person's speech, thought, and deed throughout the entire day,
that they all branch out and are drawn after the first speech,
and therefore the first speech
[and likewise thought and deed]
of a person upon rising from his sleep must be in the service of G-d,
for through this he draws holiness into all his speech, thought, and deed throughout the entire day.
And behold, specifically through this, that his inner closeness to Divinity
(during prayer)
is in such a way that he draws Divine light into his physical matters until he makes them vessels for Divinity, they reach a higher level,
as is known
regarding the matter of "and much
increase is in the strength of an ox."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The drawing down of Zeir Anpin into Malchus follows the order of external then internal drawing, and through the internal drawing that is received within Malchus, one reaches the root of Malchus which is higher than the root of Zeir Anpin.

translations.translation: And likewise it will be understood regarding the matter of drawing down Zeir Anpin into Malchus
(the union of Zeir Anpin and Nukvah),
that the order in this is
(as above in section 1)
that first there must be the external drawing down and afterward the inner drawing down.
For even the external drawing down is a very lofty drawing down
(in the manner explained above in sections 2-3),
being the level of the encompassing light that is above the chain of descent and vessels
(and therefore it is not absorbed into the Sefirah of Malchus in its inwardness, because it is above the limitation of its vessels).
But nevertheless,
this drawing down is an external level,
being only a mere illumination.
However, through the inner drawing down,
which is received in Malchus in its inwardness,
one reaches a higher level
(than the level of the encompassing light).
And the matter is,
that the root of Malchus is above the root of Zeir Anpin.
For the root of Zeir Anpin is from the externality of Keter, and the root of Malchus is from the inwardness of Keter.
And although regarding Zeir Anpin it is said,
"Zeir Anpin is attached and dependent in Atik,"
it is known that the intention is not regarding Atik itself
(only the externality of Atik).
However, the root of Malchus is in the inwardness of Atik,
which is the Radl"a.
But nevertheless,
due to its descent downward, its root is in concealment,
and the revelation of the root of Malchus is specifically through Zeir Anpin,
and through this itself, the Sefirah of Malchus is elevated above Zeir Anpin.
And this is the matter of the order of the drawing down,
that first there must be the drawing down of Zeir Anpin into Malchus in a way that the aspect of Zeir Anpin, which is above Malchus, is felt
(for specifically through it is the revelation of the root of Malchus).
But nevertheless,
since the drawing down is from the aspect
(the superiority)
of Zeir Anpin,
it has a connection to the chain of descent
[in the manner explained above
(section 3)
regarding the thirteen tikkunei dikna].
And specifically through the inner drawing down that is received in Malchus in its inwardness,
since this drawing down is from the aspect
(the superiority)
of Malchus,
therefore through it one reaches the root of Malchus, which is above the root of Zeir Anpin,
to the point that Malchus influences Zeir Anpin,
"A woman of valor is the crown of her husband."
